report: Stopped voluntarily at pastry workshop, not blocked. The roadside meal was clear and mildly satisfying. The two cultures made sense, but dough plus yeast failed twice until I learned to place both in the fermentation room; the generic failure did not explain that distinction. Once learned, yogurt was routine placement then combination. I tried fruit yogurt and buttered bread for pleasure and neither worked, which reduced my urge to experiment. The humoral menu side branch was a welcome oddity, reached with a hint, then annotated successfully. Returning to flour plus butter failed; I suspect the cool bench is required, but another place-both-and-combine sequence no longer interested me enough to continue. I did not reach the ending. This is a logical-interface impression only.

Voluntary stop after satisfying stage 3 pastry goals; not blocked. Opening causal chains were intuitive but routine. Failed dough plus yeast taught the receiving-item placement rule clearly, and I generalized it to yogurt and pastry. Optional fruit yogurt and bread and butter were the most satisfying discoveries because they answered my own ideas rather than a quota. Humoral book plus modern nutrition note failed; one hint led to the menu branch, whose abstract annotation was less rewarding than a concrete historical example would have been. Butter into flour versus dough was recognizable, but the repeated place-combine-bake pattern now feels routine. I do not feel enough curiosity to continue to snack cake today. This is one source-blind logical-interface agent playtest, not a human enjoyment claim.

Started fresh at Weather with authored baseline 43 attempts and 38 combinations excluded. Completed Weather and advanced to Relay: my delta is 20 attempts, 14 accepted, 13 combinations, 1 advance, 6 failed combinations, 4 hints. Mast plus vane and rotor install were intuitive; station becoming functional then producing a weather record and updating the map gave a coherent payoff. Most sensor preparation and installation felt like checklist work. Empty logger, temperature and pressure slots invited direct matching items, but each failed with only No new combination here. Logger wiring was inferable; thermometer louver and pressure housing needed hints. Sealed housing plus controller also failed; mesh plus housing then controller worked. Object descriptions explain combinations afterward instead of supplying useful clues beforehand. Sources remain on the board after creations, adding clutter and making parts feel duplicable. At Relay the missing crew invitation is appealing but another large maintenance cabinet suggests repetition, so I voluntarily stop rather than pursue completion. Logical agent play only, not human fun evidence. Read instructions and player output only, no scenario or source inspection.

Voluntary stop in painting workshop after optics goals and scaled architectural view. 24 attempts, 15 accepted, 13 creations, 3 hints. Enjoyed pinhole placement leading to inverted image, camera obscura, then optical experiment; this had a concrete causal thread. Perspective construction chain was legible after one failed parallel-lines plus horizon guess, but then felt routine. Generic failures for aperture plus dark room, barrier plus aperture, image plus protocol, and paint plus drawing or light study do not distinguish an incomplete setup from a bad concept. Focused image plus light ray felt like an abstract naming gate after ray already produced refraction. Projection construction explanation merely restates its ingredients. I stopped because I was losing interest in finding the prescribed intermediate noun for the painting; I wanted a visible consequence or richer feedback instead. No claim about human enjoyment or graphical interface. Did not see chance stage. Blind player protocol maintained; no source or scenario read.

Reached journey complete. Initial axe and planks chain and rope footbridge were satisfying intelligible crafts. Wheel recipe needed a hint; wheel versus axle versus planks distinctions lacked explanatory descriptions. Mill parts gave empty hints until gear existed, causing an unnecessary trip back for axle and materials. Axe plus wheel making gear then waterwheel gearing plus millstone was coherent after discovery. Flour sack and final basket were clear but routine. Bakery revived interest through a setting: cellar description suggested fermentation, but direct combinations with cellar failed; starter onto dough gave excellent exact receiving-item placement guidance. Flour plus air starter was a satisfying guess. Total 34 attempts, 25 accepted, 19 creations, 7 hints, 2 visits, 1 placement, 3 advances. Finished because this short journey had reached its ending; would not seek more generic pair filling right now. Logical-interface source-blind play only, not a claim about human fun or graphics.

Completed all three scenes. Gate and table combinations were readable and mildly satisfying, with the permission becoming a shared place at the table the strongest payoff. Stage two felt like matching abstract labels to a hidden sequence: welcome reading plus ordinary fast day and chapter 53 failed; brothers timetable plus fasting rule and host permission failed. Used two hints, which restored flow but supplied the recipe rather than helping me reason from source content. Blank source descriptions made those failures feel arbitrary. Continued because I wanted the hospitality question resolved; no urge to revisit or keep combining after the ending. Twenty attempts, sixteen accepted, twelve creations, four rejected combinations, two hints. Logical interface only; no claim about human enjoyment or visual usability.

Stopped voluntarily after completing stage 5, The mill bend, with advance available. Not stuck and not at campaign ending. Opening clay and brick, the flour-dough-flatbread sequence, bridge building and the portable crossing map were coherent discoveries. Brook was strongest: mostly self-directed construction and a meaningful record of a bridge that stays behind. Plant-to-grain required sampling hinted partners; fruit plus stone failing while fruit plus water made juice was less intuitive. Cottage requested giving a house a window, but window onto house was rejected even though both goals were complete. Mill machinery connected sensibly after making a gear, but water plus wheel failed while water plus planks made a waterwheel. By the end I felt the repeated chain-checklist-advance rhythm more than a changed inhabited place; flour was supplied before the mill existed and I never used the finished mill. I did not feel a reason to revisit earlier areas; automatic travel inventory removed the new crossing map. Five completed scenes felt like enough for this sitting; no universal human-fun claim. Logical-interface only, source blind by protocol, no graphics or touch evaluation.

Voluntary stop at provisioned refuge, stage 7 goals satisfied, not campaign ending. Fresh checkpoint play: 26 accepted actions, 23 combinations (18 creations, 5 installations), 2 advances, 1 placement; no rejected attempts, hints, undo, moves or visits. Weather observation to route map coherent; clear descriptions made combinations intuitive but often routine. Relay repeated base-plus-two-slots pattern. Missing-crew hook motivated continuation. Relay onto knoll first generated recording but left contact objective false; repeating identical drop later placed it and satisfied goal, confusing bureaucratic extra gesture. Original parts and old object states remaining after transformation felt cluttered/inconsistent with consumed installations. Rescue tow versus repair choice welcome; chose tow. Getting intact cabin to prepared refuge was satisfying; bedding and soup were literal checklist. Crew warm and fed gives enough closure to stop rather than start another chain. Logical interface trial only, no graphics or human-fun claim.

Voluntary end of sitting after completing stage 3, not the campaign ending and not a technical block. 33 attempts, 27 accepted, 25 creations, 2 advances. Opening pots gave scientific-method labels a concrete anchor; calibration limits, retaining variation and repeatability allowing disagreement were worthwhile. Early plausible combinations failed with no explanation; empty hints felt like dead-end declarations although later-created partners worked. Stage 2 was smoother and I explored ambiguity/context beyond the goals because equal payments versus equal sacrifice mattered. The valid-argument output switched from levy fairness premises to a different rule-R example, weakening continuity. Stage 3 taught the useful caveat that copying between manuscripts can defeat a simple family tree, but supplied no actual variant words or foreign word to judge. I increasingly felt I was assembling labels for intellectual work rather than doing that work. Ending this sitting because the term-plus-modifier chains have become routine. Mild curiosity about later topics remains, but no strong immediate desire to return. Logical interface only; no graphics or touch assessment.

Completed without hints or rejected gestures. Measuring cargo for a broad ferry and measuring a passage for a slim skiff was the best contrast: same wood and tools, different purpose and arrangement. Build steps were legible, but the second assembly chain felt routine, with little choice or surprise. Launch feedback was only Placed; miller payoff arrived on advance, while rescue ended with Journey complete and still-present waiting-fisher text. I continued to see the second job and ending, not because recipes were uncertain. Beyond recipes, the story conveyed that material, skilled making, shape, and intended use explain different aspects of the boat, and a sound boat is not suitable for every task. Much of that was explicitly told in descriptions rather than discovered through consequences. Logical-interface impressions only, not human-fun evidence. No desire to replay the same path.
